**Analysis date:** 2026-07-22 | **Last close (verified):** $325.89 | **Session range:** 323.34 – 329.00 | **Volume:** 38.76M

**Data consistency note:** The point-in-time OHLCV pull (2026-01-01 → 2026-07-22) and the verified snapshot agree exactly on the latest session (2026-07-22: O 327.87 / H 329.00 / L 323.34 / C 325.89 / V 38,755,900). No discrepancies to flag. All prices below are from those two tool outputs; indicator values are from the verified snapshot and the indicator time series.

---

## 1. Market context — what regime is AAPL in?

AAPL is in a **confirmed, broad-based uptrend** across all three horizons, but it is currently in a **digestion phase immediately after a fresh record-high thrust**. The important structural facts:

| Horizon | Evidence | Read |
|---|---|---|
| Long-term | Price $325.89 vs 200-SMA $275.28 → price **18.4% above**; 200-SMA has risen every session in the window (265.57 on 2026-06-08 → 275.28 on 2026-07-22) | Uptrend intact, benchmark rising |
| Medium-term | Price vs 50-SMA $304.89 → **+6.9%**; 50-SMA is **10.8% above** the 200-SMA and rising monotonically (282.21 on 2026-06-08 → 304.89) | Bullish MA stack, no death-cross risk |
| Short-term | Price vs 10-EMA $322.88 → **+0.9%**; 10-EMA (322.88) > 50-SMA (304.89) > 200-SMA (275.28) | Perfect bullish alignment |
| YTD | 271.01 (2026-01-02) → 325.89 (2026-07-22) = **+20.25%** | Strong year, with two sharp shakeouts |

The year has **not** been a straight line. Two meaningful corrections are visible in the raw data:
- **Feb–Mar 2026 slide:** 278.12 (2026-02-06) → 246.63 (2026-03-30), roughly **-11.3%**, followed by a base around 247–260 through late April.
- **June 2026 air-pocket:** 315.20 (2026-06-02) → 275.15 (2026-06-25) = **-12.7%**, including a -6.1% single session on 2026-06-25 (close 275.15, volume 107.0M).

Both declines were **recovered in full and exceeded** — the second one violently: from the 2026-06-25 close of 275.15 to the 2026-07-17 close of 333.74, AAPL gained **+21.3% in 15 sessions**. That is a powerful, volume-confirmed V-shaped recovery, and it is the dominant fact shaping the current risk/reward.

---

## 2. The most relevant indicators for this specific setup (8 selected)

I chose indicators that answer four different questions without duplicating each other: *trend direction* (moving averages), *momentum trajectory* (MACD + RSI), *volatility envelope / extension* (Bollinger bands), and *whether volume validates price* (VWMA).

**1. close_10_ema ($322.88)** — The single most actionable line right now. Price is only 3.01 points above it, so it is the tripwire separating "healthy consolidation" from "short-term trend break." It has risen every session since 2026-06-30 (289.34 → 322.88), confirming the leg is live.

**2. close_50_sma ($304.89)** — Medium-term trend spine and the reference "deep support" level. Its steady climb (282.21 on 06-08 → 304.89) proves the June dip was a pullback inside an uptrend, not a trend change. It also sets the boundary beyond which the bullish thesis needs serious re-examination.

**3. close_200_sma ($275.28)** — The strategic benchmark. Price at 1.19x the 200-SMA and the 200-SMA sloping up means the primary trend is up; this indicator is here to keep position sizing oriented to the big picture rather than to a three-day wiggle. Notably, the June low close (275.15 on 2026-06-25) was within 0.4% of *today's* 200-SMA value — the long-term mean really was tested and held.

**4. macd (8.712 vs signal 7.113)** — Momentum confirmation. The MACD line crossed above its signal around 2026-07-01/02 (histogram flipped from -1.251 on 07-01 to +0.261 on 07-02) and crossed above zero between 07-02 (-0.686) and 07-06 (+0.879). Both events fired *before* the 07-15 breakout, a textbook sequence. Today the line is still above signal, so the trend signal is unbroken.

**5. rsi (62.54)** — Overbought/oversold and, more importantly, *momentum divergence control*. RSI printed 71.43 (07-16) and 71.65 (07-17) — genuinely overbought — and has since cooled to 62.54 *without* price breaking down. That is the classic "overbought relief through time, not price" pattern in strong uptrends.

**6 & 7. boll_ub ($345.83) / boll_lb ($274.30)** — Used as a *volatility envelope*, not a signal generator. Band width is $71.53 (23.1% of the $310.06 midline) — extremely wide, i.e., realized volatility is elevated. Position of price within the bands (%B = (325.89 − 274.30) / 71.53) = **72%**, upper third but comfortably below the upper band. Critically, the upper band is expanding fast (312.31 on 07-02 → 345.83 on 07-22, **+10.7%**) while the lower band is roughly flat (277.29 → 274.30). That asymmetry is the signature of an upside volatility breakout, not a squeeze about to reverse.

**8. vwma ($319.48)** — The volume cross-check, and the most valuable signal in this report. VWMA jumped from 300.72 (07-16) to 310.27 (07-17) — a **3.2% one-session move in a volume-weighted average** — which can only happen if enormous volume traded at much higher prices. It then kept stepping up (314.02 on 07-20, 317.27 on 07-21, 319.48 on 07-22). Price sits **2.0% above VWMA**: buyers are in control, and the average *cost basis of recent volume* is chasing price upward rather than price having run away from the volume base.

**Why this set is non-redundant:** three MAs at distinct time constants (10/50/200) give trend *layering*; MACD gives momentum *direction and cross timing*; RSI gives *overbought state* (a different question than direction); the Bollinger pair gives *extension in standard-deviation terms*; VWMA gives *participation quality*. I deliberately avoided stochastics (redundant with RSI), macds/macdh as standalone selections (the histogram decline is read off the macd/signal spread), and the Bollinger midline (the 50-SMA/10-EMA already cover the "mean" role).

---

## 3. Nuance: what the data actually says about the last five sessions

This is where a naive read ("uptrend, buy") would be wrong in its details. The tape has **changed character** since the 2026-07-17 high:

| Date | Close | Volume | RSI | MACD hist | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-07-15 | 327.50 | 60.96M | 68.77 | 2.766 | Breakout day, +4.0% (from 314.86) |
| 2026-07-16 | 333.26 | 62.97M | 71.43 | 3.229 | New record close, heavy volume |
| 2026-07-17 | 333.74 | 63.41M | 71.65 | 3.337 | Peak close; intraday high 334.99; hist peak |
| 2026-07-20 | 326.59 | 53.47M | 63.87 | 2.724 | -2.14% reversal day, low 323.68 |
| 2026-07-21 | 327.74 | 41.34M | 64.54 | 2.214 | Inside day, low 322.22 |
| 2026-07-22 | 325.89 | 38.76M | 62.54 | 1.599 | Range 5.66 (< ATR 8.02), lowest volume of last 5 |

Three things stand out:

1. **Momentum is decelerating, not reversing.** MACD histogram has fallen from 3.337 (07-17) to 1.599 (07-22), a **-52% decay** in four sessions, and the MACD line itself rolled from 8.927 (07-21) to 8.712. RSI dropped 9.1 points from its 71.65 peak. Yet price is only **-2.35%** off the record close. That is distribution *of momentum*, not *of shares* — but it does raise the probability that the next 1–3 weeks are sideways-to-lower rather than an immediate breakout continuation.

2. **The pullback is happening on shrinking volume — a constructive tell.** Volume fell from 63.41M (07-17) to 38.76M (07-22), three consecutive declines. Supply is not aggressive. A distribution top usually shows *rising* volume on down days; here 07-20's -2.14% came on 53.47M, below the 63.41M of the prior up day.

3. **The 10-EMA is holding as the short-term floor.** The 07-21 low of 322.22 came within $0.01 of that day's 10-EMA (322.21), and price closed above it; 07-22's low of 323.34 also held above the current 10-EMA of 322.88. Three consecutive closes (327.74, 325.89) above a rising 10-EMA is the definition of an intact short-term trend. A decisive close below 322.88 would be the first objective evidence of trend degradation and would shift the tactical bias to neutral.

---

## 4. Levels that matter (all traceable to tool output)

**Resistance / upside references**
- **$333.74** — record close, 2026-07-17 (and $334.99 intraday high, same day). This is the line that must be reclaimed to reassert breakout momentum.
- **$345.83** — current Bollinger upper band (2026-07-22). With band width expanding, this is a *dynamic* ceiling: it was 312.31 on 2026-07-02 and has risen ~10.7% in three weeks. It is not a target per se, but it defines how much room a continuation move has before becoming statistically stretched.
- **$326.59–$327.74** — the 07-20/07-21 closes; immediate overhead supply from the reversal week.

**Support / downside references**
- **$322.88** — 10-EMA. First line; loss of it = short-term trend break.
- **$322.22** — 07-21 low, effectively coincident with the 10-EMA (confluence).
- **$314.86–$317.31** — the 07-14 / 07-13 closes, i.e., the pre-breakout consolidation shelf. A retest here would be a normal, non-thesis-breaking pullback.
- **$310.06** — Bollinger midline (20-SMA). Mean-reversion magnet if momentum keeps fading.
- **$304.89** — 50-SMA. The medium-term trend line; the level at which the bullish structure requires reassessment.
- **$274.21–$275.15** — 2026-06-25/06-26 lows and long-term mean zone (200-SMA now $275.28). Far away, but it is the line in the sand for the primary trend.

---

## 5. Actionable interpretation and risk management

*(ATR value below is taken from the verified snapshot: ATR (14) = $8.02, ≈2.46% of the $325.89 close — elevated versus $6.79 on 2026-06-08, consistent with the expanding Bollinger width.)*

**Base case — bullish consolidation, higher highs likely over 4–8 weeks.** The stack (10-EMA > 50-SMA > 200-SMA, all rising), the positive MACD/signal spread, the VWMA stepping up $30 in three weeks, and an expanding upper Bollinger band all point the same way. RSI at 62.54 leaves room before the 70 zone is re-entered.

**Tactical plan (swing horizon):**
- **Constructive trigger:** a close above **$329.00** (today's high) followed by a close above **$333.74** re-establishes the breakout. Confirmation would be volume back above the 07-17 figure of ~63M and MACD hist turning up from 1.599.
- **Preferred entry zone for trend followers:** hold/add while price stays above the **$322.22–$322.88** confluence. Scaling in on a tag of the 10-EMA rather than chasing 07-17 highs is the higher-expectancy approach given the -52% histogram decay.
- **Second-chance entry:** **$314.86–$317.31** shelf — a controlled pullback to the pre-breakout base with VWMA still rising would be healthy, not bearish.
- **Invalidation (short-term):** a daily close below **$322.88** with expanding volume → reduce tactical longs; bias neutral between there and the Bolly midline.
- **Invalidation (medium-term):** a daily close below **$304.89** (50-SMA) → the 10>50>200 stack is broken; stand aside.
- **Stops:** roughly **1.0–1.5× ATR = $8–12** below entry. For a long initiated near $326, that implies a stop in the **$314–$318** region — conveniently aligned with the structural shelf, i.e., the stop is placed where the chart says "I'm wrong," not at an arbitrary distance.
- **Position sizing:** with ATR at 2.46% of price and band width at 23% of the midline, this is a **high-volatility regime**; size positions ~25–35% smaller than you would in the June range-bound tape (ATR $6.79–$7.00 on 2026-06-18/06-24) to keep dollar risk constant.

**What would flip me cautious:** (1) a break of $322.88 on rising volume; (2) MACD line crossing back below its signal (needs a further ~1.6-point decline in the spread); (3) price failing at $333.74 a second time on *declining* volume; (4) VWMA flattening or rolling over while price churns — that would mean the high-volume 07-15/07-17 buyers are no longer adding.

**What would make me more aggressive:** a quick reclaim of $333.74 accompanied by volume ≥ 70M and MACD hist re-expanding above 2.5, which would convert the current pause into a classic bull-flag continuation.

---

## 6. Summary table

| Price | Close / Range / Volume | $325.89 / 323.34–329.00 / 38.76M | Consolidation | -2.35% from 07-17 record close, on shrinking volume |
| Short-term trend | close_10_ema | $322.88 | Bullish (price +0.9%) | Rising 12 straight sessions; 07-21 low 322.22 held it |
| Medium-term trend | close_50_sma | $304.89 | Bullish (price +6.9%) | Rising since 06-08 (282.21→304.89); 10.8% above 200-SMA |
| Long-term trend | close_200_sma | $275.28 | Bullish (price +18.4%) | Sloping up; June low close 275.15 ≈ tested it |
| Momentum direction | macd / signal | 8.712 / 7.113 | Bullish, decelerating | Bull cross ~07-01/02, zero cross 07-02→07-06; line rolled off 8.927 (07-21) |
| Momentum strength | macdh | 1.599 | Weakening | -52% from 3.337 peak (07-17) in 4 sessions |
| Overbought state | rsi | 62.54 | Neutral-bullish | Cooled from 71.65 (07-17) without a price break — healthy |
| Volatility envelope | boll_ub / boll_lb | $345.83 / $274.30 (mid $310.06) | Expanding to upside | %B = 72%; width 23.1% of midline = high-vol regime |
| Volume confirmation | vwma | $319.48 | Strong bullish | Price +2.0% above; VWMA +3.2% in one day on 07-17 |
| Risk unit | atr | $8.02 (2.46% of price) | Elevated | Stops $8–12; trim position size ~25–35% |

**Bottom line for AAPL:** The primary and intermediate trends are unambiguously up — every moving average is rising and correctly stacked, MACD remains above its signal, and VWMA's steep ascent shows the July breakout was volume-backed. What has changed in the last four sessions is the *rate* of progress: MACD histogram down 52%, RSI off 9 points, and volume contracting for three straight days. That combination most often resolves as **consolidation before continuation** rather than a top, which argues for holding core longs with a stop beneath the $314–$318 shelf and adding on either (a) a volume-confirmed reclaim of $333.74 or (b) a controlled dip into the $315–$318 base — rather than chasing strength into a fading momentum tape.

## 2. AAPL-specific material events (July 21 ET)

### 2a. Apple raises Apple Music subscription prices — Services pricing power
- **Published:** 2026-07-21 19:53:47 UTC = **15:53 ET**, Yahoo, [link](https://finnhub.io/api/news?id=c3e02113009d026a57b59507b63015eefa9bf54e8396853491cc5342c0eff7d9)

Against that: the stated cause is *rising licensing costs*, so the revenue lift may be partly offset at the gross-margin line; and a price hike in a competitive streaming market carries a small churn risk.
- **Impact:** mildly positive, small magnitude at the consolidated level (Music is a minor slice of Services). Horizon: 1 quarter (revenue recognition) rather than 1 day.
- **Uncertainty:** Low on the fact, medium on the financial materiality — no subscriber base, price elasticity or margin figure was disclosed in the evidence.

### 2b. Klarna lease-to-own programme for iPhone, iPad, Mac
- **Published:** 2026-07-21 18:18:43 UTC = **14:18 ET**, Yahoo, [link](https://finnhub.io/api/news?id=c55fc65f6882fd5156789079143e6543b77c17a286b9fb0ed3601562ed773716)
- **Evidence (summary):** "lease-to-own program for iPhones, iPads, and Macs… a big change for the hardware company, and comes as it looks to raise prices on many of its products."
- **Read:** Two distinct signals in one headline. (i) **Demand elasticity management** — third-party leasing lowers the entry cost of hardware that is getting more expensive, which supports unit volumes and upgrade cadence. (ii) **A price-increase signal on hardware** — a more consequential datapoint than the Music hike, implying management sees room (likely tariff/component-cost driven) to push ASPs up.
- **Impact:** modestly positive for hardware revenue and ASP mix over 1–2 quarters; risk that financing partners capture economics and that stretched consumer credit conditions blunt the benefit. Horizon: 1–6 months.
- **Uncertainty:** High. No terms, revenue-share, attach-rate or launch geography were provided; "big change" is the *source's* characterisation, not a disclosed financial fact.

### 2c. EU Digital Markets Act — US lawmakers intervene

Bearish interpretation: escalation raises the probability of retaliation cycles and adds a policy overhang to a stock already carrying antitrust exposure. This is *advocacy*, not a rule change — no court ruling, no Commission decision.
- **Impact:** near-zero expected fundamental effect in the next week; mainly affects the risk premium and headline flow around EU decisions. Horizon: 1–12 months.
- **Uncertainty:** High. No timeline, no named legislators' bill, no EU response in the evidence.

### 2d. TSMC price increases — indirect input-cost pressure
- **Published:** 2026-07-21 18:27:00 UTC = **14:27 ET**, Yahoo, [link](https://finnhub.io/api/news?id=ad27e0581b144661c4d1ffbefac647fabdaf5c9b78be58ed086e12e19bc64b2b)

This dovetails with the hardware price-increase language in 2b (raising prices to offset cost) — a coherent but *unconfirmed* narrative. Note the article frames the pain as AI-capex-related, which is more directly a hyperscaler issue than an Apple one.
- **Impact:** mildly negative for gross margin at the margin; likely offset by pricing. Horizon: 2–4 quarters.

**Net read for the 2026-07-22 session: mildly constructive but low-conviction.**

2. **Two small positive company catalysts landed in the same afternoon** (Music pricing at 15:53 ET, Klarna leasing at 14:18 ET). Both are directionally favourable to revenue/ASP and both fit a single coherent management narrative: **raising monetisation and pushing hardware prices while softening the affordability shock for consumers.**
3. **That narrative is exactly where the two-sided risk sits.** Higher hardware prices + rising rates + "energy tensions" (per the 16:09 ET Nasdaq piece) is an uncomfortable combination for a consumer-hardware franchise. If the Klarna programme is a response to demand softness rather than a pure ASP upgrade, the read flips negative.
4. **Regulatory overhang (DMA) is the one item capable of a sharp move**, but it is advocacy, not enforcement — I assign it a low near-term probability of material re-rating.
5. **Sector correlation risk is elevated in both directions** per the MAGS piece; the Mag-7 "rut" framing means the stock is unlikely to be rescued purely by index strength.

**Horizon mapping:** intraday-to-1-week effects are dominated by tape and Mag-7 earnings sentiment (Alphabet/Tesla Wednesday per the evidence) rather than by anything Apple disclosed. The pricing, leasing and foundry-cost items matter over **1–6 months** and should be reflected in estimates, not in a single session. The DMA item is a **multi-quarter** policy variable.

**What would change my mind (not in this evidence):** any confirmed hardware price list, Klarna programme terms, an EU Commission action, Apple's own earnings date/guide, or any July 15–20 news — all of which the supplied 20-record slice leaves open.

## 7. Synthesis: What the Fundamentals Actually Say

**Bull case (evidence-based)**
1. **Revenue re-acceleration to +16% YoY for two consecutive quarters** (H1 revenue $254.9B), a step-change from the FY2023–FY2025 profile.
2. **Gross margin at a dataset high of 49.3%** in Q2 FY2026, up 220 bps YoY — mix and pricing power intact.
3. **Operating margin at 34.0% H1** despite a 32.6% R&D surge — the company is funding an investment cycle out of operating leverage, not sacrificing profitability.
4. **H1 FCF of $78.3B** (+33% normalized), capex at just 1.7% of revenue — exceptional cash conversion.
5. **Net cash rebuilt to ~$62B** (+$28B in six months); gross debt −14%. Balance sheet is strengthening, not deteriorating, while still returning $44.7B.
6. **Equity up 44% in six months** ($73.7B → $106.5B), AOCI improving.

**Bear case / risks to monitor**
1. **Tax rate structurally higher at 17.5%** (vs 15.0–15.5%) — a permanent ~2.5pt drag on EPS growth relative to pre-tax growth.
2. **Buyback pace cut 25%** and share count shrinking only 0.71%/half — removes a key historical EPS tailwind. Consensus models that assume a ~2–3%/yr float shrink are too high.
3. **Working-capital release is not repeatable**: $22.5B of AR/nontrade-receivable/payable unwind flattered H1 CFO; expect reversal.
4. **Cash-tax benefit is non-recurring**: +$11.3B YoY benefit to CFO will not repeat.
5. **$12.8B of new intangible assets** appeared with no discrete acquisition line — an unexplained M&A/asset purchase that carries integration and future amortization risk.
6. **R&D +32.6% with no visible revenue attribution yet** — if the step-up does not convert into product-cycle revenue, margins compress.
7. **No June-quarter filing yet** as of 2026-07-22 despite Apple's pattern of late-July Q3 reports — event risk is concentrated in the coming days.
8. **Data gap:** no insider-transaction archive, and no price data in the tool set, so **valuation multiples (P/E, EV/FCF, FCF yield) cannot be computed from what was returned** — any multiple quoted to you from another source should be checked against these TTM-adjacent figures (H1 EPS $4.85, H1 FCF $78.3B, net cash $61.9B).

**Actionable positioning read:** The filings describe a company that is **growing revenue mid-teens, expanding gross margin, aggressively funding R&D, and rebuilding net cash while moderating buybacks.** That combination is fundamentally constructive, but the *EPS* optics are deliberately being held back (tax rate up, R&D up, buyback slower). Traders should distinguish between **business momentum (strong/accelerating)** and **per-share EPS leverage (decelerating vs. prior years)**.
